faulting_instructions.meaning: reads the FileSystem pointer out of the engine and then dereferences it

root_cause: I passed FileSystem = nullptr. Engine::Initialize stores it without checking, and LocalizationManager::InitializeLanguage later dereferences it as this+0x358.
retraction: My earlier statement that FileSystem may be null was based on the fact that the 3049-byte Initialize body only writes [this+0x358] and never reads it. That is true of that body, but the subsystems it calls do read it. The conclusion was too narrow and is withdrawn.
bonus_finding: The four trailing std::string parameters belong to LocalizationManager::InitializeLanguage(string const&, string const&, string const&, string const&). They are the four localisation names, not per-subsystem settings.

what_worked_before_the_crash.window: WinWindow + Initialize returned 1 and produced a real HWND
what_worked_before_the_crash.settings: default constructor produced the direct3d11 name with length 10; an explicit +0x0c value was accepted
what_worked_before_the_crash.engine: Engine::Engine produced the expected vtable at base+0x33E2F0
what_worked_before_the_crash.publish: global_before=0x0, global_after=<engine pointer>, so the host-side publish itself worked
what_worked_before_the_crash.call: Engine::Initialize was entered and ran until the localisation step

fix_to_try: Construct a real FileSystem with FileSystem::FileSystem() at 0x86370 and pass it instead of null.
not_claimed: that a FileSystem constructed in isolation is usable
that the next crash will not occur
